## [Remove the two measured transfer stalls: per-piece fdatasync and Nagle on peer streams](ROADMAP.md#remove-the-two-measured-transfer-stalls-per-piece-fdatasync-and-nagle-on-peer-streams) `@templartorrent.milestone.loopback-throughput/1`

### Prove the batched sync against power loss with a fault-injected disk

`proposed` · `@templartorrent.work.power-loss-batched-sync/1` · part of `@templartorrent.milestone.loopback-throughput/1`

Close the open gate on the batched write path (milestone loopback-throughput dropped the per-piece fdatasync): show that a resume bitmap written at a checkpoint names only pieces the checkpoint's sync made durable, so a power loss after the checkpoint cannot leave a trusted bit over bytes that never reached the disk. The forced-kill test could not show this because the page cache survives a killed process. Add a disk observer seam to the storage crate, a shadow that models durable versus volatile bytes, and a driver test that loses power after a checkpoint, restores the durable image with the checkpoint's mtimes, restarts from the record and completes with matching bytes; and a negative control that forges one lost piece into the bitmap and shows the resulting hole, proving the harness can tell.
